name: useHiLight
summary: The eight-LED ring around the rear camera flash. Real LEDs or nothing.
plain: Controls the coloured lights around the rear camera. Useful as a glanceable signal when the phone is face down: a colour for an incoming call, a pulse while an assistant is thinking. Either it drives the physical LEDs or it reports that it cannot; there is no on-screen substitute.
description: Android 17 exposes the array as eight lights of type Light.LIGHT_TYPE_APPLICATION, but every lights session needs CONTROL_DEVICE_LIGHTS, which is signature|privileged and cannot be held by a normal app. PixelKit therefore ships a small Java daemon that runs as the adb shell user and listens on 127.0.0.1:11080; start it with npm run hilight:daemon. With the daemon up, availability is hardware and the calls drive real LEDs. Without it, availability is unavailable and every control function refuses: it resolves false and sets error. Nothing is mirrored on screen. mode, isActive and currentColor change only after the daemon answered a command with a 2xx status.

returns.name: availability
returns.desc: Whether calls reach the LEDs ('hardware'), the daemon is not running ('unavailable'), or this device has no array.

returns.name: isHardwareSupported
returns.desc: Whether this device physically has the LED array.

returns.name: isDaemonConnected
returns.desc: Whether the local daemon answered its last status check, polled every five seconds.

returns.name: isActive
returns.desc: Whether the ring is currently lit.

returns.name: currentColor
returns.desc: Active colour as a hex string.

returns.name: mode
returns.desc: Pattern label: off, glow, breathing, pulse, gemini_thinking, incoming_call or notification.

returns.name: brightness
returns.desc: 0 to 1, sent to the daemon with the next lit command. The initial 0.85 is the hook's default request, not a value read from the LEDs.

returns.name: source
returns.desc: Where the numbers came from. There is no 'simulated' value: a reading is real, derived from real readings, or unavailable.

returns.name: error
returns.desc: Latest failure message from a refused or failed control call, or `null` after the next accepted command.

actions.name: refreshDaemonStatus()
actions.desc: Re-checks the daemon immediately instead of waiting for the next five-second poll.
actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon answered, false otherwise. The same value lands in isDaemonConnected.

actions.name: setColor(hex)
actions.desc: Sets a solid colour and turns the ring on, switching the mode from off to glow when needed. Refuses when the daemon is not connected.

inputs.name: hexColor
inputs.desc: RGB hex string such as "#81C995". Sent to the daemon as-is together with the brightness.

actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon accepted the command; currentColor, mode and isActive update only then. Resolves false and sets error otherwise.

actions.name: setMode(mode, hex?)
actions.desc: Switches the animation pattern, optionally with a colour sent in the same daemon command. Refuses when the daemon is not connected.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.desc: One of off, glow, breathing, pulse, gemini_thinking, incoming_call, notification. Passing 'off' extinguishes the ring.

inputs.name: hexColor
inputs.desc: RGB hex colour to light the pattern with. Defaults to currentColor. Ignored for 'off'.

actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon accepted the command; mode, isActive and (when lit) currentColor update only then. Resolves false and sets error otherwise.

actions.name: setBrightness(level)
actions.desc: Sets the brightness sent to the daemon. While the ring is lit the level is sent immediately; while it is off the level is kept for the next lit command.
actions.output: While lit: true when the daemon accepted it, false and error otherwise. While off: true, because nothing is sent until the next lit command.

actions.name: triggerGeminiPulse(ms?)
actions.desc: Cyan gemini_thinking hold that clears itself. Pair it with a model call. Refuses when the daemon is not connected.

inputs.name: durationMs
inputs.desc: How long to hold before clearing, in milliseconds. Defaults to 4000. The same duration is sent to the daemon.

actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon accepted the command; a timer from an earlier hold is cancelled then and a new one starts. Resolves false and sets error otherwise.

actions.name: triggerContactAlert(hex, ms?)
actions.desc: Coloured incoming_call hold for a caller or event, then clears itself. Refuses when the daemon is not connected.

inputs.name: hexColor
inputs.desc: RGB hex for the alert colour.

inputs.name: durationMs
inputs.desc: Hold time in milliseconds. Defaults to 5000.

actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon accepted the command and replaces any hold already running. Resolves false and sets error otherwise.

actions.name: turnOff()
actions.desc: Sends the off command and cancels any pending auto-off timer.
actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon accepted it; mode becomes off and isActive false only then. Resolves false and sets error otherwise.

actions.name: toggle()
actions.desc: Switches between off and a default blue glow. Refuses when the daemon is not connected.
actions.output: Resolves true when the daemon accepted the command and isActive flipped. Resolves false and sets error otherwise.

agentNote: Read availability before promising light. Only 'hardware' drives the LEDs; 'unavailable' means the daemon is not running and the control functions resolve false and set error rather than pretending. Check the boolean the call returns before telling the user the light is on.
